One is covetous, thinking regarding the wealth and equipment of others, "Oh, may what belongs to another be mine." One is of a malicious mind and corrupt intent, thinking, "May these beings be slaughtered, bound, annihilated, destroyed, or may they not exist at all." One holds wrong views and a perverted outlook, thinking, "There is no merit in almsgiving, sacrifice, or offerings. There is no fruit or result of good or evil deeds. There is no this world and no other world. There is no mother, no father, and no beings reborn spontaneously. There are no recluses or brahmins in the world who, having realized this world and the other world through their own direct knowledge, make them known."

Monks, possessing these ten qualities, one is placed in hell as if brought there.

3. Monks, one possessing ten qualities is placed in heaven as if brought there. Which ten?

4. Here, monks, a certain person, having abandoned the taking of life, abstains from taking life. He dwells with the rod laid aside and the weapon laid aside, modest, compassionate, and mindful of the welfare of all living beings. Having abandoned taking what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given. Regarding the wealth and equipment of another in the village or forest, he does not take it as a thief would. Having abandoned sexual misconduct, he abstains from sexual misconduct. He does not engage in relations with those who are protected by mother, father, brother, sister, relatives, or lineage, those who follow the law, those who have husbands, those who face penalties, or even those crowned with a garland of flowers. Having abandoned false speech, he abstains from false speech. When summoned to a council, an assembly, a meeting of relatives, a guild, or a royal court, and asked to testify by saying, "Come, good man, tell us what you know," if he does not know, he says, "I do not know," and if he knows, he says, "I know." If he has not seen, he says, "I have not seen," and if he has seen, he says, "I have seen." Thus, he does not speak falsehood for his own sake, for the sake of another, or for the sake of some trivial gain.

<note>Footnotes from the original text: 1) T. M. read "vatāyam"; M6 reads "vata ayam." 2) M6 and S read "va." 3) Omitted by S. 4) S reads "viparitta." 5) T. M6 and M add "ti." 6) T. M6 and M read "tan nādinnam"; Ph. and S read only "adinnam." 7) Ph. and S read "na āḍo." 8) M continues: "pa || antamaso." 9) Ph. inserts "mātāpitu." 10) Ph. inserts "gotta." 11) Omitted by T. M6 and M.</note>

<summary>This passage details ten unwholesome states of mind and conduct that lead to rebirth in lower realms, followed by the commencement of a list of ten wholesome practices that lead to rebirth in heavenly realms.</summary>
